bracket: [Textbook misprint: the chapter gives the H-O-H bond angle THREE different values, and they cannot all be right. §5.3 prints \(104^\circ 35'\); Table 5.5, whose whole purpose is to list bond angles, prints \(104^\circ 28'\); and the table of Ex Q.6 prints \(104.5^\circ\) (which is \(104^\circ 30'\)). The three differ by up to 7 arc-minutes. Which one is the misprint cannot be settled from the chapter itself, so the answer below quotes \(104^\circ 35'\), the value the running text of §5.3 derives when it explains the reduction from the tetrahedral angle. Any of the three should be accepted.]

[Textbook note (not an error): the chapter states the H-N-H bond angle of ammonia two ways — §5.3 gives \(107^\circ 18'\) when it explains the reduction from the tetrahedral value, while Table 5.5 lists it simply as 107 (that table prints no degree symbol on any of its three entries). The answer below uses the rounded \(107^\circ\), which is also the value printed in the stem of Ex Q.3 (G).]

[Textbook misprint: the bond-angle column of this table disagrees with the chapter's own text for water. The table prints \(104.5^\circ\) for \(\mathrm{H_2O}\), while §5.3 gives \(104^\circ 35'\) and Table 5.5 gives \(104^\circ 28'\) — three different values for one angle. The completed table below reproduces the \(104.5^\circ\) the question itself supplies. For \(\mathrm{NH_3}\), where the angle is left blank, the answer uses \(107^\circ\) from Table 5.5; §5.3 gives \(107^\circ 18'\) for the same angle.]
